data.name: Lúcia Taveira
data.bio: Lúcia cooked in hotel kitchens for twenty years before opening Ervalume in her grandmother's old shop. She writes the menu every afternoon from what the market had that morning.
data.imageAlt: Portrait from the chest up of a chef in a linen apron in her kitchen, copper pans hanging behind her, smiling.

data.name: Caio Brandão
data.bio: Caio runs the dining room, keeps the book of tables and makes the drinks, most of them with fruit and herbs from the same stalls as the kitchen.

data.heading: The kitchen
data.body:
Everything at Ervalume is cooked over wood: a grill for fish and vegetables, and a brick oven that is lit at six in the morning and still warm at midnight. Gas is used for one thing, the coffee.

Lúcia buys at the street market twice a week and from two farms on the edge of the city on the other days. The menu changes when the market does, so a dish on this page may be gone by the time you visit, and something better may have taken its place.

data.heading: A restaurant made up to show a real product
data.body:
Ervalume is invented. The restaurant, its address, its people and its dishes do not exist, and no table here can be booked. It is a sample site for Viglet Shio, the open-source CMS, installed from one marketplace package.

The photographs were generated for the package and are free to redistribute with it. The fonts are Fraunces and Plus Jakarta Sans, both under the SIL Open Font Licence and served from the site itself.

data.heading: How booking works
data.body:
The dining room has eleven tables, and we keep four of them for people who walk in. Tell us the day, the time and how many of you are coming, and Caio answers by email within a day to confirm the table or offer the nearest time we have.

We hold a booked table for fifteen minutes. For a group of more than eight, or to take the whole room, write to mesa@ervalume.example.

data.heading: Ask for a table
data.intro: We answer within a day. A request is not a booking until we write back to confirm it.

data.heading: Find us
data.body:
Ervalume is on the corner of Rua das Laranjeiras and the Largo do Alecrim, two blocks from the street market. Look for the green doors and the pots of herbs on the pavement.

The street is closed to cars on Sundays. The nearest bus stop is on the square, and there is a bicycle rack by the door.

data.title: Cooking over wood
data.description: Ervalume is a small neighbourhood restaurant that cooks everything over wood, with herbs and produce from the street market two blocks away.
data.heading: Cooked over wood, seasoned from the market
data.intro: A small dining room on the Largo do Alecrim, a wood fire and a menu written every afternoon from what the market had that morning.
data.imageAlt: An empty dining room set for the evening, a row of wooden tables under brass lamps, pots of rosemary and basil on the window sill and a wood oven glowing at the back.
data.storyText: Lúcia is at the stalls by seven. Coriander, chillies, cassava and whatever fish came in overnight decide what the fire cooks that evening.
data.storyImageAlt: A market stall with a wooden crate of coriander and basil, bundles of chives, a basket of red chillies, cassava roots and limes.

data.title: Menu
data.description: Starters, mains and desserts cooked over wood at Ervalume, with prices.
data.intro: Written this afternoon from what the market had this morning. Prices include service.
data.note: Tell us about any allergy when you sit down. Most dishes can be made without nuts, dairy or gluten if we know in time.
